cost: $4000 (subframe swap, new a-arms, new wheels, new tires, new alignment, new shock)
entry:
After a month of downtime while Clint at Gas Head Motorworks swapped a front subframe due to an incident where I was run off the road and into a curb, I finally got her back! And she even has a set of shiny new '94 hollow-spoke wheels! New tires too—we decided to go with the Falken SINCERA SN250 A/S, a 720-treadwear all-season tire which had the best overall rating on TireRack.com, knowing full well that they will age out in 5 years and require replacement long before the tread ever wears out.

The drive home from Clint's shop was an interesting one, to say the least... We had a Mazda Comp shock on the front temporarily while I was waiting for the Xida XL replacement shock to arrive, and the tires were brand new, and the car was running a shoestring alignment just to get it home. So I was being super careful as the spongy tires darted and moved all over the road with almost no grip, as the mold release was still intact. And of course, it had to start raining on the drive back.

But all of that didn't matter. Even the slight amount of drifting I did on the exit ramp from Highway 290 onto 610 North didn't faze my happiness in driving the old girl again. It quite literally brought a tear to my eye.

After another 3 weeks, I finally got her replacement Xida XL shock in from 949 Racing, and I was able to get her back on the road after another visit to Clint to get the new shock installed and the alignment done. I have to say, I missed her a lot. I'm glad to have her back.

Here we are at the close of the year, and as you can tell from the mileage not much has changed for Miyoshi. There are several issues still at large; the exhaust has a leak where the header meets the catalytic converter, and the AC system still has issues in warm weather. So the car has mostly sat garaged this year, only being driven on nice days when the weather is cool enough to not tax the AC system too much.

 Now we have entered the winter season (or what passes for winter here in Houston) and I am using the car more and more as the AC can keep up on days below 80 degrees and the heather works just fine for cooler days. It's also the only Miata I have on all-season tires that I don't have to worry about driving on cold mornings and ruining a set of super 200 race tires.

 I have a tune-up planned for it in January to replace the spark plugs and wires, and I am considering replacing the exhaust system with a new cat-back system to fix the exhaust leak and adding a functional catalytic converter again (it would be nice to have a quieter exhaust again). Other than that, I am just enjoying having Miyoshi around again after a year of limited use.

cost: $1250 (New catalytic converter, new head unit, new speakers, transmission and differential fluid change)
entry:
True to my word, I bought a new catalytic converter and had it installed which did a great job of quieting down the car and also fixed a really nasty exhaust leak.
There wasn't much point in wasting a trip to the shop for just one item though, so I decided to splurge a bit and had several more items checked off my list.

First item up was maintenance related, change the differential and transmission fluid, and change the clutch and brake hydraulic fluid. I had been putting this off for a while, and it was definitely overdue. The car felt much smoother and more responsive after the fluid change, and it was nice to have fresh fluid in the clutch and brake systems as well.

![New ](/images/na/blog/headunit-01.jpg)

Next up was the audio system. The head unit in the car was pretty old and outdated, and the speakers were in pretty rough shape from two seperate water incidents.
 I went with the Millenium 5 kit which had two door speakers, 4 headrest speakers, and the headrest boxes that were surprisngly missing from my car. These speakers are direct plug and play replacements. While I was there, my mechanic pointed me to a modern head unit on Amazon for a whopping $65 dollars after coupon to replace the ancient Pioneer system I had originally installed back in 2004. This new head unit of undetermined origin (probably China) has full bluetooth connectivity and android auto, so I can easily stream music from my phone and use Google maps now.

The sound quality certainly won't set the world on fire, and the shortcomings of a sound system in a 91 Miata from the 90s is very apparent. No sub-woofer, no real amp so to speak, just the head unit and what the speakers can muster. But it's still better than nothing, the unit dims when I turn my headlights on and android auto switches to night mode, and the touch screen makes it a easier to use system than the OEM Mazda head unit in my 2023 Miata.

Next up on the list, the old girl was looking a little shabby, definitely needed a bath and it was time for another paint clean and wax.
Well, good idea in thoery, in practice a single-stage repaint that is 20 years old and led a hard life isn't going to be the easiest to work with. I washed the car to get any loose containmenants off the paint, then I went to using Meguirar's ultimate compound with my orbital buffer, which ended up becoming a splotchy mess withe the oils fromt he product not evenly distributed across the paint due to the deteriorating paint condition.
 I ended up having to go over the entire car panel by panel with distilled water ina  spray bottle and two microfiber towels to andequately remove the excess oils and product from the paint, which was a very time consuming process. After that, I went over the car with Meguiar's ultimate wax, which went on much better and was much easier to work with than the compound. The end result was a much shinier car, but the paint has reached "preservation-mode" where it will be cleaner-wax and maintenance washes from here on out, and any further compounding or polishing will just be a waste of time and product and could potentially do more harm than good to the paint. But at least the car is looking better than it has in a while, and it's still a looker for sure.
